title: Spec Area Intent (specs/<name>.intent.json)
description: GENERATED by `tools/spec_source.py schemas --write` from area.schema.json — edit that file, then regenerate. The part of an area a model cannot say: kind, purpose, brief, scope, boundary, vocabulary, externals, assumptions, decisions, open questions, state machines, architecture, configuration. Requirements, invariants, properties, constants and examples are NOT here: they are `///` doc comments on the declarations in specs/<name>.qnt that realize them. Ledgers (verdicts, pins, logs, traceability, triage) are in specs/<name>.records.json.

kind.description: area: functional area (default) — may carry UI blocks (screens/ui_components/navigation); UI-specific lint, readback, and codegen trigger on block presence, not kind. contract: cross-area invariant carrier, spec-only, requires spans[].

area.description: Slug, also the filename stem: specs/<area>.<kind>.json. Examples: auth, billing, auth-ui, user-permission.

spans.description: Areas this spec depends on. Contracts: the 2+ areas the contract joins (required). Areas with UI blocks: the area(s) whose state the surface reads (e.g. ['auth']).

purpose.description: One paragraph: what this area is responsible for.

brief.description: Authored prose that orients a human before the machine-checked detail. The ONE long-form thing an agent writes into the readback — everything else there is derived from fields. Prose cannot be checked the way a witness can, so it carries a freshness pin instead: `written_against` records the spec sha it was written for, and spec-lint flags it once the spec moves. Rendered verbatim and marked as narrative rather than verified fact, so the readback stays byte-identical for identical input.

text.description: Lead paragraph(s), Markdown. If it needs its own headings it is competing with the generated sections instead of introducing them.

how_it_fits.description: Optional facet: the area's shape — main entities, how they relate, the flow through them. The orientation a new reviewer lacks.

why_this_way.description: Optional facet: the reasoning behind the shape. Complements decisions[], which record what was decided but not the narrative joining them.

watch_out_for.description: Optional facet: the sharp edges — what is easy to get wrong, which requirements interact, where the open questions bite.

author.description: Who wrote it. A human-written brief is not re-authored by the agent without asking.

boundary.description: The SUBSTITUTION boundary: what would have to stay identical for a different implementation of this area to be a drop-in replacement. `scope` says what the area is responsible for; this says what 'the same' means. Without it, 'the regenerated code matches' has no referent — and the differential runner has nothing to compare. Most valuable on brownfield areas, where an implementation already exists and can serve as the oracle.

entry_points.description: The callable surface clients depend on, with argument shape: 'login(email, password)'. A replacement must accept these.

observable_state.description: What a client can read back and therefore can notice changing. These are what the differential comparator diffs after each step — typically the same abstractions the conformance adapter's getters expose.

persistence_contract.description: Whether the stored representation is part of the contract, and how much of it. The one people forget: behavior can match perfectly while a regenerated schema orphans every existing row. State it explicitly, including 'none — the store is private and may be replaced'.

emits.description: Outward signals other systems consume — events, webhooks, audit records. Observable whether or not anyone calls them API.

free.description: Deliberately NOT preserved: file layout, log wording, internal structure, algorithmic approach. Naming these is what keeps the spec a specification rather than a transliteration — a spec that pins everything can no longer disagree with the code, so it inherits its bugs as truth.

scope.description: The declared semantic boundary. Completeness is only meaningful relative to a boundary: without one, 'closed' is an unbounded claim nobody can check, and every OUT-OF-SCOPE triage verdict is an unfalsifiable assertion. Declaring it turns both into checkable statements — the readback's ship verdict reads 'READY relative to this scope', and spec-lint requires an OUT-OF-SCOPE cell to name the exclusion that covers it.

included.description: Capabilities this area is answerable for, in domain words (cart, checkout, payment authorization).

excluded.description: Capabilities deliberately NOT covered. Each needs a reason: an exclusion without one is indistinguishable from an oversight.

reason.description: Why it is out: owned by another area, deferred, or genuinely not this product's job.

owner.description: The area or team that owns it instead, when there is one.

pass.description: Brownfield: this slice of the area's code is DEFERRED to that extraction pass, not excluded for good. spec-extract-audit lists every deferred exclusion with the sites triaged OUT-OF-SCOPE against it, so the next pass starts from them. A reason starting 'Deferred to pass N' reads the same.

concepts.description: Vocabulary: entities, actors, verbs. The 'what we're talking about' layer that informs the formal model.

closed.description: CLOSED WORLD: states[] is exhaustive — no other externally meaningful state exists, and no other may be invented downstream. spec-lint then requires the sidecar's variant type to have exactly these constructors (no more, no fewer), so an LLM adding a state to the model, or code adding one to an enum, is caught rather than absorbed. Leave false/absent for a set that is genuinely open to extension.

actors.description: Who/what can initiate actions: User, Admin, System, ScheduledJob, etc.

verbs.description: Domain actions: login, charge, expire, etc. Loose — gets refined into Quint actions during formalization.

externals.description: External systems this area depends on, with the FULL set of outcomes each can produce. Declaring them turns 'what if the payment provider times out?' from a question nobody asked into a matrix cell that must be covered or triaged. An external with no declared outcomes is an idealized dependency — the most common place real-world semantics go missing.

outcomes.description: Every outcome the dependency can produce, INCLUDING the unhappy ones (DECLINED, TIMEOUT, NETWORK_ERROR, DUPLICATE). Each becomes a row in the external×outcome completeness matrix.

terminal.description: True when the outcome ends the interaction (no retry/poll can follow).

assumptions.description: Environment facts the specification RELIES ON but does not establish. First-class because a verification result that depends on an unstated assumption overclaims: the readback annotates every invariant an assumption bears on, so a ✓ reads 'holds, given ASM-001' rather than 'holds'. Never silently treat an external system as ideal — write the idealization down here.

statement.description: The assumed fact, stated so it could in principle be falsified. 'PaymentProvider eventually responds', not 'PaymentProvider is reliable'.

kind.description: 'unrepresentable' is the sharpest case: something the MODEL cannot express and therefore cannot be wrong about — monotonic clocks, atomic increments, single-writer storage, bounded skew. The model is silent on it by construction, so silence must not be mistaken for coverage.

external.description: The externals[].name this assumption is about, when it is about one.

affects.description: IDs whose verification depends on this assumption (INV-NNN, PROP-NNN, REQ-NNN). The single direction of the link — invariants do not list their assumptions, so there is one source of truth. Drives the readback's 'under ASM-NNN' annotation.

status.description: 'accepted': believed and relied upon. 'accepted-risk': known to be possibly false, shipped anyway — requires a `rationale` saying who accepted it and why. 'open': undecided, blocks approval. 'retired': no longer relied upon.

rationale.description: Required for status 'accepted-risk'. An assumption knowingly carried as risk needs its argument recorded, or the next reader cannot tell a considered bet from an oversight.

discharged_by.description: How the assumption is monitored or tested in the real system, if it is (an alert, a contract test). Absent means: believed, not checked.

decisions.description: ADRs. kind='architecture' entries pair with the architecture section to record WHY non-obvious choices were made.

affects.description: IDs this decision governs (REQ-NNN, INV-NNN, CON-NNN, or <area>.<ID> across areas). When the decision changes, this is the blast radius — the list spec-diff reads to say which obligations a reversal puts back in play. spec-lint FAILs a dangling reference.

state_machines.description: Explicit state machines for stateful entities. Optional but valuable: spec-lint validates structural completeness (unreachable states, dangling non-terminal states, transitions referencing undeclared states, Quint mutations not listed as transitions) without needing Apalache. /spec-readback renders the diagram from this section. Each entry corresponds to one entity from concepts.entities[] that has states[].

entity.description: Entity name. Must match a concepts.entities[].name.

quint_var.description: Quint var that holds this state in the sidecar (used by spec-lint to cross-check).

quint_type.description: Quint variant type defining the state values.

initial_state.description: The state the entity is in after `init`. Must appear in states[].

name.description: State name; matches a variant constructor in quint_type.

terminal.description: No outgoing transitions expected. Lint warns if a terminal state has any.

lifecycle_actions.description: Quint actions that mutate quint_var but aren't state transitions on an existing instance — creation, destruction, garbage collection. Suppresses the 'sidecar action mutates quint_var but isn't listed as a transition' warning for these. Example: login creates a Session in initial_state, so it goes here, not in transitions[].

from.description: Origin state (must be in states[]) or '*' meaning 'from any non-terminal state'.

trigger.description: Action or event name; usually matches a Quint action.

actor.description: Who or what initiates the transition: User, Admin, System, etc.

guard.description: Plain-language precondition. The Quint action encodes the formal version.

quint_action.description: Name of the Quint action that realizes this transition. spec-lint checks the sidecar mutation of quint_var matches the transitions listed here.

architecture.description: Per-area architecture (Layer 0-6 except diagrams). Sparse: only declares overrides from project defaults in .spec/project.json. inherits_project=true (default) merges; false makes this fully standalone.

implements.description: Quint action names this component implements.

architecture_file.description: Optional sidecar specs/<area>/components/<name>.json with a fuller per-component architecture.

module_layout.description: Path templates. Variables: {area}, {component}, {ext}. Paths relative to code_root resolved from .spec/project.json.

cross_cutting.description: logging, metrics, tracing, auth, feature_flags. Each is a string or object.

quint_file.description: Sidecar path, e.g. 'auth.qnt' (relative to this JSON). The Quint module is the source of truth for the formal spec; module name and imports are read from it directly via tools/quint_ir.py — never mirrored here.

probe_domains.description: Finite domain each action PARAMETER TYPE is drawn from in the generated stepP, as a Quint set expression: {"UserId": "Set(\"alice\", \"bob\")"}. Keyed by type rather than by parameter name because types are stable while parameter names vary per action. Required by tools/spec-probes.py and deliberately not inferred: how much of the state space the probes explore is a scope decision — too small and a probe cannot fire, too large and every check pays for it — so it is stated in the spec rather than guessed by a generator. A key of the form `param:<name>` targets one parameter by name and wins over its type's key — for a model whose parameters all share one type (every id a `str`). Prefer a type alias per value domain (`type Role = str`); use `param:` where an alias would be noise.

ghost_zeros.description: Explicit initial value of a probe ghost, keyed by TYPE as written in the model: {"Result": "Ok"}. tools/spec-probes.py builds the zero of base types, maps, sets, lists, tuples, records (field by field, aliases resolved) and sum types (their first variant) on its own; this is for a type it cannot build (parameterized, recursive) or whose first variant is the wrong zero. Wins over the synthesized value.

probes_file.description: Generated probe module, e.g. 'auth.probes.qnt' (relative to this JSON). Contains the ghost-instrumented step wrapper and the path-constrained witness probes. Regenerated by /spec-check; never hand-edited.

alloy_file.description: OPTIONAL structural sidecar, e.g. 'user-permission.als' (relative to this JSON). Hand-written Alloy holding the relational/structural checks for this area — typically a contract. Behavior stays in the Quint sidecar; Alloy answers structure-shaped questions (cardinality, referential integrity, ownership) without paying the temporal product cost. Only invariants marked `proof: "structural"` are routed here.

conformance.description: Model-based conformance testing config: how witness traces are replayed against real code. /spec-code-generate generates the adapter and harness; /spec-code-verify runs the command and treats a requirement as verified only when its witness trace replays green.

adapter.description: Path (relative to code root) of the adapter mapping Quint actions to code API calls and Quint vars to observable code state.

harness.description: Path (relative to tests root) of the trace-replay harness that loads ITF files and drives the adapter.

command.description: Shell command that replays all traces, e.g. 'pnpm test conformance'. Run from the code repo root by /spec-code-verify.

pbt_command.description: OPTIONAL stateful property-based testing command. Apalache returns the SHORTEST counterexample, so replay is a handful of traces and a handful of steps per area, each requirement exercised once. The adapter already exposes one method per action, one getter per var and a reset() — which is exactly a stateful-PBT interface, so the same adapter drives thousands of randomized sequences for the price of wiring. Complements replay, never replaces it: replay checks the model's own traces, PBT explores beyond them. The zero-new-code option is quint's own simulator: `quint run --mbt --n-traces=1000 --out-itf=traces/pbt/out.itf.json <area>.qnt` writes out<N>.itf.json traces carrying mbt::actionTaken and mbt::nondetPicks — the same action-plus-arguments the probe module's _last* ghosts carry, so the existing adapter consumes them unchanged (itf_tools.action_params reads both conventions).

traces_dir.description: Where witness traces live, relative to specs/. Default: '<area>/traces'.

differential.description: DIFFERENTIAL conformance, available only to brownfield: the existing implementation is an oracle that answers any question you ask it, and until you ask, extraction fidelity is asserted by a human rather than measured. The comparator instantiates the SAME adapter twice — once over the original, once over the regenerated implementation — drives both through identical sequences, and diffs boundary.observable_state after every step. Each divergence is either a missing spec element (the extraction gap you were hunting) or an intentional difference (record it as a decision).

parallel_path.description: Where /spec-code-generate --parallel writes the regenerated implementation. NEVER the original's path: the oracle has to survive the experiment.

command.description: Shell command running the comparator. Exit 0 = no sequence distinguished the two.

sequences.description: How many randomized sequences the comparator should run. Reported with the verdict, because 'equivalent' means 'no counterexample in N', never 'equivalent'.

source.description: Where the question came from: matrix, matrix-orphan, red-team:critical, red-team:important, counterexample, elicitation, …

states.description: Visible states: idle, loading, error, etc.

visible_when.description: Plain-language condition or Quint predicate name.

witnessDelta.description: The PRE-state the witnessing step must start from. A postcondition alone proves reachability, not causation: a guard that already implies its own postcondition makes the action a no-op that only fires once its result already holds, and the probe goes green over dead text. The probe conjoins this over `_prev*` ghosts snapshotted before the step, so the trace must show the state actually MOVING. Referenced from BOTH the witness (a `must` has one) and each permitted outcome (a `may` proves each outcome with its own probe, so each names its own pre-state) — tools/spec-probes.py reads outcomes[].delta, which this schema previously forbade outright.

pre.description: Quint boolean over the `_prev*` ghost vars, true exactly when the pre-state was one this behavior could still change. For a lockout: `_prevAccountStatus.get(_lastUid) == Unlocked`.
